title: feat(editor): track element creation timestamps
body:
separated from https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/11847

Elements have a last-update timestamp but no independent creation time. This adds `created: number | null`, the client-clock creation time in epoch milliseconds of an element instance, and keeps `createdBy` / `updatedBy` and author-credit rules for a follow-up PR.

### Behavior

- New elements and copies with new IDs (duplicate, paste, library insertion) get a fresh creation timestamp. This describes the new instance, rather than the age of its source content.
- Edits, history capture, undo/redo and conversions that retain identity preserve the existing timestamp. Autoshape recognition preserves it while retaining the same element type/ID; replacing the element with a different type starts a new lifetime.
- Restoring a scene preserves known timestamps and maps missing values to `null`. An unknown creation time stays unknown: neither load time nor `updated` can reliably reconstruct it. Explicit `null` and `0` are preserved.

### Design decisions

Creation metadata is assigned during construction or duplication, before Store snapshot/delta capture. This keeps the live element and captured revisions consistent and avoids making capture time the birth time of an element created earlier in a gesture or stream. It requires no Store stamping, additional version bumps, transaction changes or author-credit machinery. The timestamp is descriptive metadata; collaboration conflict resolution continues to use the existing versioning rules.

`ElementUpdate` excludes `created`, making ordinary timestamp edits a type error. An explicit metadata repair must construct a replacement revision. Deltas still carry the field for replay, but creation-metadata-only differences do not count as visible changes or create separate undo steps.

Compatibility follows the conventions for other added element properties. Existing restore boundaries normalize incomplete runtime data, while import/export types, the `restoreElements` signature and the `updateScene` contract retain their existing shapes. A `created`-only optional input type or normalization shim would imply a special legacy-input guarantee for one field. General typing of raw import data belongs in a consistent, separate change. Hand-written complete element objects now need `created`, using `null` when unknown; existing scenes need no bulk backfill.

Freedraw, iframe and embeddable skeleton conversion now uses the standard constructors, so retained-ID inputs also receive defaults while preserving explicit timestamps. Regenerated IDs receive a fresh timestamp before construction. Label and endpoint fragment options exclude `created` because these fragments are constructed as new instances.

### Related boundary changes

- PNG scene embedding and JSON clipboard export restore their inputs, matching the existing canvas/SVG paths. All four paths are tested with legacy elements missing `created`.
- File loading restores elements once and uses that same result for scroll-to-content calculations. This also means imported-scene centering uses normalized geometry; bounds can differ when restore repairs or removes input elements.

### Validation

- Full suite: `yarn vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1` — 125 files passed; 1,912 tests passed, 47 skipped, 1 todo.
- `yarn test:typecheck` passed.
- ESLint with `--max-warnings=0` passed on all changed TypeScript files.
- Coverage includes construction, duplication, skeleton conversion, legacy restore, library import, export, history, gesture creation and autoshape recognition; serialized snapshots and JSON schema documentation include the field.

(implemented by gpt-6-astra; unslopified by fable-5-1 and me)
